entities.summary:
The Russo-Japanese War was a pivotal conflict between the Russian and Japanese empires from 1904 to 1905, fought primarily in Manchuria. This clash of powers took place in the context of a rapidly changing global landscape, as European empires were expanding their reach into Asia.

The war began on February 8, 1904, when the Japanese launched a surprise attack on the Russian naval base at Port Arthur. The conflict saw the involvement of prominent military leaders, including Admiral Heihachiro Togo and General Yevgeni Alekseyev. The war was marked by several key battles, including the Battle of the Yellow Sea and the Battle of Tsushima. The war ultimately ended on September 5, 1905, with the signing of the Treaty of Portsmouth.

The Russo-Japanese War had significant consequences for the region. It led to the weakening of the Russian Empire and the strengthening of Japan, which would go on to play a major role in the early 20th century. The war also marked the beginning of the end of the imperial era in Asia, as nationalist movements began to rise in countries such as China and India.

The war's legacy can be seen in the subsequent rise of Japan as a major world power, as well as the decline of the Russian Empire. The war also had a profound impact on the development of modern warfare, with the introduction of new technologies and tactics.

As Admiral Togo famously said, 'The Russo-Japanese War was a war of attrition, and we won it by being more resourceful and adaptable than our enemy.'
